summary.en: Use a queue to discover one distance layer at a time and recover an unweighted shortest path.
summary.bn: কিউ দিয়ে এক স্তর করে গ্রাফ ঘুরে দেখো, আর কম এজের পথ বের করো।

notes: The BFS examples use fixed arrays because the graph always has seven vertices. C17 does not supply a built-in queue type. The head and tail variables implement this traversal queue without dynamic allocation.

sections.title: Explore nearby vertices before distant ones
Trace the queue on the shared diamond
Read distances and reconstruct a route
Why first discovery gives a shortest route
Separate traversal work from construction work
Preserve the meaning of first arrival

examples.title: Queue traversal with distances and parents
examples.explanationHtml: The queue visits 0,1,2,3,4,5. Vertex six stays unreachable. Vertex five gets parent three because three is processed before four.

examples.title: Reverse parent links to recover a route
examples.explanationHtml: Walking parents gives 5,3,1,0. Printing this temporary path backward gives a three-edge route from zero to five.

examples.title: An isolated start still discovers itself
examples.explanationHtml: The start has distance zero and no parent even when its adjacency list is empty. No other vertex enters the queue.

practice.title: Label distances from a chosen source
practice.statementHtml: Read graph 0..3 and start 0..6 using the four graphs in this lesson. Print the graph/start prompt, order: and dequeue IDs, then v distance=D parent=P for IDs 0..6. Use ascending neighbors, -1 for unreachable distance and for the source parent.
hints: Distance minus one also acts as the undiscovered flag.

practice.title: Recover the BFS route
practice.statementHtml: Read graph, start and target within the same bounds. Print Graph, start and target:, the order: line, then no path or path: followed by source-to-target IDs.
hints: Stop the backward walk at parent -1, not at vertex zero.

practice.title: Trace queue layers
practice.statementHtml: On graph zero from source zero, give the queue after expanding each reachable vertex.
hints: Mark on enqueue to avoid duplicates.
practice.answerHtml: Initially [0]. Expanding 0 gives [1,2]; expanding 1 gives [2,3,4]; expanding 2 gives [3,4]; expanding 3 gives [4,5]; expanding 4 gives [5]; expanding 5 gives []. Vertex 4 is not added again when reached from 2.

practice.title: Prove shortest hop distances
practice.statementHtml: Why can BFS assign a final distance when a vertex is first enqueued?
hints: Assume a shorter route and inspect its predecessor.
practice.answerHtml: The FIFO queue processes nondecreasing distances. When u first discovers v, every earlier layer has already been expanded. A shorter route to v would have an earlier-layer predecessor, which would already have discovered v. Therefore dist[u]+1 is the minimum hop count.

quiz.prompt: When should BFS mark a newly found vertex?
options: Only when dequeuing the second copy
quiz.explanation: Early discovery prevents duplicate queue entries from different predecessors.

quiz.prompt: Why does BFS use a FIFO queue?
options: It always selects the largest ID
It expands earlier distance layers before later ones
quiz.explanation: New vertices are one layer beyond the vertex currently expanded.

quiz.prompt: What does dist[v]=-1 mean after source BFS?
options: v is unreachable from that source
quiz.explanation: All reached vertices receive nonnegative hop counts.

quiz.prompt: Do BFS parent links necessarily give the only shortest path?
options: Yes, shortest paths are always unique
No, ties depend on neighbor order
quiz.explanation: The first discovery selects one predecessor among possibly equal-length alternatives.

quiz.prompt: Does ordinary BFS find minimum total cost with arbitrary unequal weights?
options: Yes, every queue is a priority queue
Yes, if all vertices are marked
Only if the source ID is zero
quiz.explanation: Unequal edge costs require an algorithm that accounts for weights.

quiz.prompt: Why can the one-shot example queue hold at most V entries ever?
options: Every graph has only V edges
Each vertex is enqueued at most once
A matrix forces a queue of length one
quiz.explanation: Mark-on-enqueue bounds total append operations as well as active queue size.

quiz.prompt: What must you do with target-to-source parent links before printing a forward route?
quiz.explanation: Parents walk backward through the selected BFS tree.

quiz.prompt: After two FIFO removals, which queued vertex is removed next?
quiz.explanation: The next removal reads index two.

quiz.prompt: What distance is assigned to a newly discovered neighbor of a distance-two vertex?
quiz.explanation: A discovery edge adds one hop to its predecessor distance.

quiz.prompt: How many parent links separate vertex three from source zero?
quiz.explanation: The links are 3 to 1 and 1 to 0.

quiz.prompt: What is the BFS helper cost with adjacency lists, excluding the demonstration builder?
quiz.explanation: Each active neighbor entry is inspected once, and vertex arrays are initialized once.

keyPoints.en: Mark a vertex when it enters the BFS queue.
keyPoints.bn: বিএফএস কিউতে ঢোকানোর সময়ই ভার্টেক্স মার্ক করো।

keyPoints.en: Each queued vertex has its final unweighted distance.
keyPoints.bn: কিউতে ঢোকা ভার্টেক্সের কম এজের দূরত্ব তখনই ঠিক হয়ে যায়।

keyPoints.en: Parent links form a tree over reachable vertices.
keyPoints.bn: প্যারেন্ট লিংকগুলো পৌঁছানো যায় এমন ভার্টেক্স নিয়ে একটা ট্রি বানায়।

keyPoints.en: Unreachable vertices keep distance minus one.
keyPoints.bn: পৌঁছানো যায় না এমন ভার্টেক্সের দূরত্ব মাইনাস এক থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Adjacency-list BFS scans O(V+E) entries in total.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যাডজেসেন্সি লিস্টে বিএফএস মোট O(V+E) এন্ট্রি দেখে।

examQuestions.answerHtml: Initially [0]. Expanding 0 gives [1,2]; expanding 1 gives [2,3,4]; expanding 2 gives [3,4]; expanding 3 gives [4,5]; expanding 4 gives [5]; expanding 5 gives []. Vertex 4 is not added again when reached from 2.

examQuestions.answerHtml: The FIFO queue processes nondecreasing distances. When u first discovers v, every earlier layer has already been expanded. A shorter route to v would have an earlier-layer predecessor, which would already have discovered v. Therefore dist[u]+1 is the minimum hop count.

examQuestions.question: Trace queue traversal with distances and parents for input: 0 0. Show the intermediate memory or worklist changes.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The queue visits 0,1,2,3,4,5. Vertex six stays unreachable. Vertex five gets parent three because three is processed before four.

Graph (0..3) and start (0..6):
order: 0 1 2 3 4 5
0 distance=0 parent=-1
1 distance=1 parent=0
2 distance=1 parent=0
3 distance=2 parent=1
4 distance=2 parent=1
5 distance=3 parent=3
6 distance=-1 parent=-1

examQuestions.question: Write the BFS discovery loop for one vertex u using the arrays in the lesson. Explain why enqueue happens only once per vertex.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
for (int j = 0; j < degree[u]; j++) {
    int v = adj[u][j];
    if (dist[v] == -1) {
        dist[v] = dist[u] + 1;
        parent[v] = u;
        queue[tail++] = v;
    }
}

Assigning distance before enqueue marks the discovery. A later predecessor sees a nonnegative value and skips the same vertex. The loop costs O(degree(u)) time and no extra allocation.
